item.title: Michigan lands commitment from Indiana QB Landon Hall, who threw 51 touchdowns in 13 games
item.description: Landon Hall was in Ann Arbor last weekend for the Michigan Wolverines’ 18-16 triple-overtime win over the then-No. 4 UCLA Bruins, the only loss on UCLA’s 10-1 record. He left with a scholarship offer from the coaching staff after the game and committed to Michigan on Wednesday. The Class of 2027 quarterback from Penn High School in Indiana told Hayes Fawcett of Rivals that he picked the Wolverines over the Miami (OH) RedHawks and the Eastern Michigan Eagles. Fawcett lists him at 6-foot-3 and 210 pounds. BREAKING: Class of 2027 QB Landon Hall has Committed to Michigan, he tells me for @Rivals The 6’3 210 QB chose the Wolverines over Miami (OH) and Eastern Michigan He threw 51 TDs in 13 games this season https://t.co/G5wSIf7Dn4 https://t.co/ljTrJ2gNGY — Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) November 25, 2026 Kyle Whittingham Warned by Urban Meyer About the Next-Level Intensity of the Michigan-Ohio State Rivalry (Imagn Image) Hall has put up a program-record 3,283 passing yards and 51 touchdown passes in 13 games for Penn this season, and he has completed 77.4% of his throws while doing it. All of it came in Class 6A, Indiana’s largest classification. Rivals rates Hall a three-star prospect and the No. 30 player in Indiana’s 2027 class, and his offer list before Michigan stepped in was built around programs such as Eastern Michigan and the Butler Bulldogs. He visited the Indiana Hoosiers in early November before making the trip to Michigan Stadium. Hall started his high school career across the state line at Lakeshore High School in Michigan before transferring to Penn ahead of his junior season, when he led the Kingsmen to a 6A sectional title. He becomes the second quarterback in Michigan’s 2027 class, the first full recruiting cycle under head coach Kyle Whittingham. Four-star Kamden Lopati committed to the Wolverines after backing out of his pledge to the Illinois Fighting Illini, and he holds close relationships with Whittingham and offensive coordinator Jason Beck from their time at Utah. ESPN ranked Lopati as the No. 2 quarterback in the cycle at the time. Where Lopati came in with the national ranking, Hall comes in on a senior season productive enough to draw a Big Ten offer late in his recruitment, giving Michigan two different kinds of bets at the same position in one class. A state title shot comes before Ann Arbor Penn (13-0) meets top-ranked Brownsburg (13-0) for the IHSAA Class 6A state championship at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Friday at 7 p.m. ET. Penn earned its spot by winning the 6A semi-state at Carmel High School on Nov. 20. Brownsburg brings a 32-game winning streak into the matchup and is ranked 16th nationally by MaxPreps. Penn is playing in the state finals for the first time since 2017, and a win would give the program its first state title since 2000. Hall goes into it with his college decision already made. Related Readings: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans took Josh Heupel’s golf ball suggestion against Lane Kiffi

item.title: USC president makes decision on Trojan Marching Band after members vandalize UCLA football facility
item.description: Letters went missing overnight Tuesday from the sign outside the UCLA Bruins’ Wasserman Football Center, and by Wednesday night the president of the University of Southern California had traced the damage to members of his own school’s marching band. What remained on the side of the building spelled out a lewd phrase, and photos of it were circulating online before the morning was over. A UCLA student reported the vandalism to campus police, the Daily Bruin’s Amanda Velasco reported . USC President Beong-Soo Kim then announced in a letter that the Trojan Marching Band will not perform before the game or at halftime when the USC Trojans visit UCLA at the Rose Bowl on Saturday. Administrators and band leadership made the decision together, and Kim presented it as a show of respect toward UCLA and time for the band to reflect. Jan 2, 2023; Arlington, Texas, USA; A view of the USC Trojans helmets and Cotton Bowl logo during the game between the USC Trojans and the Tulane Green Wave in the 2023 Cotton Bowl at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports “This conduct runs contrary to USC’s values and is unacceptable. We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. “We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA’s campus last night has no place in this tradition,” Kim wrote . USC’s Tommy Trojan statue and UCLA’s Bruin Bear are usually wrapped and guarded before the game, and USC students have spray-painted UCLA statues, including the Bruin Bear and the John Wooden statue, in past years. This case involves members of a university-sanctioned group, and the consequence falls on every member of the band, including those who had no part in it. UCLA’s entire statement to the Daily Bruin was “Go Bruins” and “Beat SC!” A Rose Bowl meeting with Big Ten title stakes UCLA enters Saturday at 10-1 and No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and a win keeps its path to the Big Ten Championship Game in its own hands. USC sits at No. 15 with three losses and can still get to the Dec. 5 title game in Indianapolis, but the Trojans need a win and help from elsewhere in the conference. Jul 29, 2022; Los Angeles, CA, USA; A detailed view of UCLA Bruins helmet during Pac-12 Media Day at Novo Theater. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports It is also the first meeting between the two programs as ranked teams since 2022, when No. 7 USC beat No. 16 UCLA 48-45 at the Rose Bowl. This year’s game will be played without the band that normally takes the field before kickoff and at halftime. Kim said any student found responsible will face discipline under university policy, and that interim actions are already being taken while the investigation continues. Related Readings: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans took Josh Heupel’s golf ball suggestion against Lane Kiffin

item.title: Baylor targets UTSA HC Jeff Traylor and could finalize deal before week’s end
item.description: The Baylor Bears went looking for a head coach with deep Texas roots after firing Dave Aranda on Oct. 25, and their search is now focused on Jeff Traylor of the UTSA Roadrunners. USA TODAY Sports’ John Brice reported Wednesday that Baylor is expected to move forward with Traylor before the end of the week, barring something unforeseen. Brice cited nine people with knowledge of the search, a group that includes college coaches, NFL assistants and agents. No deal has been finalized. On Tuesday, On3’s Pete Nakos reported that Traylor had emerged as the top contender while Baylor kept talking with other candidates. Bears Issue Stadium Ultimatum to Illinois Amid Indiana Relocation Threat (Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images) Brice’s sources said the search was aimed at candidates with Texas ties from the outset, and Traylor is a Texas native whose coaching career has played out almost entirely inside the state, including a high school run at Gilmer that produced a 175-26 record before he moved into the college game. At UTSA, he is 60-28, with four seasons of nine or more wins in seven years, three straight bowl victories and no losing records. His teams won two Conference USA championships before the program moved to the American, and he was twice named the league’s coach of the year. The Bears also met with top coordinators and sitting head coaches, a list that included Dan Mullen of the UNLV Rebels, and Robert Griffin III was part of the process as well. Three of Brice’s sources said the 2011 Heisman Trophy winner, who has never coached, pushed hard for the job at his alma mater. Griffin made his interest public after Aranda was fired following a 25-24 loss at the Kansas Jayhawks, saying he was “100%” interested and had already spoken with athletic director Doug McNamee . Nov 16, 2024; Morgantown, West Virginia, USA; Baylor Bears head coach Dave Aranda (right) talks with West Virginia Mountaineers head coach Neal Brown after a game at Mountaineer Field at Milan Puskar Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ben Queen-Imagn Images The Roadrunners host the Tulsa Golden Hurricane on Friday leading the American Conference, and a win clinches a place in the league championship game. UTSA can still reach the title game with a loss. Traylor will be getting his team ready for that game while the program in Waco works toward a deal with him. Under contract terms he owes UTSA $4 million if he leaves for another FBS job before Dec. 31, 2026. item.title: Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition for Democracy has confirmed that the Second Summit of Nigeria’s opposition political parties will hold on Monday in Abuja, with participating parties expected to adopt three foundational documents. The coalition is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP). In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, it said the decision was reached on Wednesday night at the seventh meeting of its Central Leadership Committee. The statement said the leaders reached the decision “following extensive deliberations on the state of the nation, the prevailing political environment and the earlier resolution to suspend campaign activities on day of the Summit”. The leaders, however, made it clear that the suspension does not end inter-party engagement. “The leaders agreed that the suspension of campaign activities does not preclude the continuation of consultations and engagements among opposition political parties on matters of common interest, including electoral integrity, democratic participation and institutional reform,” the statement said. The documents to be considered and adopted are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme. They were developed by working groups made up of representatives of the constituent parties after the inaugural summit of August 31, 2026. According to the statement, “the documents set out proposed mechanisms for inter-party cooperation and a framework for addressing national governance challenges.” The coalition leaders also reaffirmed their commitment “to working collectively to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and protect the sanctity of the ballot across the country”. The coalition invited other opposition political parties to participate in the summit and “contribute to the ongoing consultations”. Three personalities will address the summit on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”. They are the Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, HRH Oba Oladipo Olaitan; Prof. Ango Abdullahi; and Chief S. N. Okeke. The statement said the summit is expected to bring together “national leaders of opposition political parties, elected representatives, former public officeholders, civil society leaders, representatives of the media, and observers from foreign diplomatic missions in Nigeria”. item.title: Tennessee’s DeSean Bishop, Arion Carter questionable for Vanderbilt game with CFP berth at stake
item.description: The two Tennessee Volunteers players who left Saturday’s 27-13 win over the LSU Tigers banged up are both listed as questionable for the regular-season finale at the Vanderbilt Commodores on the SEC’s first availability report of the week. Running back DeSean Bishop and linebacker Arion Carter, both Walter Camp Player of the Year semifinalists, were Tennessee’s only additions to Wednesday’s report. Bishop leads the SEC with 1,215 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns, and his 110.5 rushing yards per game are the league’s best . He was named a Doak Walker Award finalist on Nov. 24, and his 248 carries rank second nationally. Against LSU, he ran 18 times for 52 yards before a lower-body injury knocked him out in the fourth quarter. Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop (18) is stopped by Arkansas defensive lineman Quincy Rhodes Jr. (97) in an NCAA college football game on Oct. 11, 2025, in Knoxville, Tennessee. “Looked good this morning. We’ll figure it out as we go through the week, just like we do with all our guys,” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel said of Bishop at his Monday news conference. If Bishop cannot go, Javin Gordon is next on the depth chart with 261 rushing yards in seven games, followed by Justin Baker. Gordon finished the LSU game after Bishop went down. Quarterback George MacIntyre, who has shared snaps with freshman Faizon Brandon and played through a right knee injury against LSU, was not on the report. Carter, a senior captain, left the LSU game in the second half with an ankle injury after piling up 10 tackles, a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery, making him the third SEC player in two decades to reach all four of those marks in one game. He plays on a defense that leads the nation with 47 sacks and leads the SEC with 22 forced turnovers. Tennessee LB Arion Carter and RB Desean Bishop are questionable for Saturday against Vanderbilt. https://t.co/7BeLDSECVb https://t.co/IOanVo4lO0 — Pete Nakos (@PeteNakos) November 26, 2026 Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) is hit by Tennessee Volunteers linebacker Arion Carter (7) resulting in an interception by defensive back Will Brooks (35) during the first half of the College Football Playoff first round game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Dec. 21, 2024. A College Football Playoff berth is on the line in Nashville Tennessee (9-2, 6-2 SEC) is No. 5 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and a win over Vanderbilt would likely secure the program’s second playoff berth in three seasons and put a home playoff game at Neyland Stadium within reach. The Vols could also reach the SEC Championship Game on Dec. 5 with some outside help. Vanderbilt (4-7, 1-7 SEC) has no postseason at stake, but the Commodores beat Tennessee 45-24 in Knoxville last season, and quarterback Jared Curtis is expected to play through a left wrist injury from last week’s 34-27 loss at the Florida Gators. item.title: Man City handed major appeal update as potential Premier League expulsion hangs over Arsenal title clash
item.description: Manchester City v Ipswich Town - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester City have received a significant update regarding the timeline for their appeal against a series of Premier League financial charges. As the club prepares for a high-stakes encounter with title rivals Arsenal, the off-pitch legal battle is reaching a critical junction that could define their future. December hearing dates emerge for City's appeal Following October's verdict finding them guilty of 114 Premier League financial breaches , Manchester City face a decisive pre-Christmas hearing. An independent commission ruled that the club used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise over £830 million in funding between 2009 and 2018 while making "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate" the investigation. City denied wrongdoing and appealed immediately , with a result initially expected in early 2027. However, former club financial advisor Stefan Borson expects clarity much sooner. Borson outlines expedited pre-Christmas timeline Speaking on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan, Borson outlined the expected hearing schedule and the league's push for a swift resolution: "We're told that it will be mid-December," Borson said. "Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th. It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time. "I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season." Why the Premier League wants to avoid fresh legal challenges An unsuccessful appeal could bring a fine, points deductions, or Premier League expulsion. To avoid fresh procedural disputes, Borson believes both sides have likely compromised on the timetable despite rulebook updates introduced at the start of the campaign. "In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable," he explained. "In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable. I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away. "The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one." Title race pressure mounts ahead of Arsenal showdown On the pitch, City's title hopes have suffered a major blow. item.title: Fifa hit by cyberattack amid mounting scrutiny of Gianni Infantino
item.description: World football’s governing body, Fifa , has been targeted in a cyberattack that compromised what it describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it confirmed on Thursday. "Fifa is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement," the organisation stated in a message. Fifa did not reveal when the cyberattack occurred or provide the precise nature of the breached data. Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were Fifa files. Three days later, the group appeared to take credit when responding to a post stating that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked. The three candidates up for election as FIFA president, Gianni Infantino, Kohzo Tashima and Philippe Diallo (AP) "FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the governing body said in its statement. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned." The breach occurs at a time when Fifa and its president, Gianni Infantino , face heightened scrutiny following a foiled, secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino is also attempting to extend his 11-year presidency of Fifa to 2031 . He remains the favourite when the election is held on March 18, with Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France standing as the other candidates.

item.title: Marching Orders: USC Band Barred From Rose Bowl Over ‘Lewd’ Vandalism Scandal
item.description: The Southern California marching band performs before an NCAA college football game against Michigan State, Saturday, Sept. 20, 2025, Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Jessie Alcheh) They say the show must go on — but one college football team’s marching band has pranked itself right out of a massive pregame performance in a big rivalry game. The University of Southern California has barred its own marching band from playing Saturday at the iconic Rose Bowl, where the school’s football team is set to take on rival UCLA in a major college football matchup. The long-running rivalry between the schools typically results in pranks, but this year’s bit was too much for USC President Beong Soo-Kim , who took the drastic step of banning his own school’s band from performing Saturday after they reportedly took letters from a sign outside of their competitor’s campus and used them to spell out “a lewd phrase,” according to ESPN. Kim issued a letter explaining the decision, writing: “This conduct runs contrary to USC’s values and is unacceptable. We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway.” ESPN reported: One of those actions is the decision not to have the band’s on-field performances at the Rose Bowl on Saturday “out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university’s values,” per Kim. “We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community,” Kim said. “Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA’s campus last night has no place in this tradition.” The game is a big one, as it’s the first time the two schools have played against each other in football as ranked teams since 2022. The UCLA Bruins are currently ranked No. 9, while USC is 15th. The post Marching Orders: USC Band Barred From Rose Bowl Over ‘Lewd’ Vandalism Scandal first appeared on Mediaite .

item.title: Gazzaniga: "The most important thing was to build a team and be all together."
item.description: Gazzaniga: "The most important thing was to build a team and be all together." Paulo Gazzaniga has highlighted the unity within Girona's locker room. The red-and-white goalkeeper values the team's current moment beyond the results: "Not just because of the results, but also because of what you can see: the unity, the team, and the effort we put into every match." Gazzaniga believes there is still room for improvement in their play, but he feels that the work to build team spirit is already evident on the pitch: "But the most important thing was to build a team and be united, and I think that has been visible for several matches now." The goalkeeper also explained how he uses his position to help his teammates. From behind the central defenders, he can follow movements like the forwards' runs, which are not always as visible from other areas of the field: "I’m lucky to see the whole field, and maybe that gives me a bit more of an advantage when it comes to communicating with my teammates." Gazzaniga also reflected on his four years at Girona: "I’m very happy and grateful to have been here these four years." The goalkeeper recalls that last season was the most difficult, but he doesn’t think it overshadows the good moments he has experienced at the club. He arrived in Girona at the age of 30 and values having been able to play matches, gain minutes, and acquire experience. From his daily routine, he cherishes the simplest things: "I think the routine is what I like the most: coming to train, seeing my teammates, and enjoying what we do." The Argentine also took a moment to talk about his family. He mentioned that when he arrived in Girona, his eldest son was one year old. Now he is five and has a younger brother who is one year old. Gazzaniga recalled the role of his father, who was also a goalkeeper, and explained that just as he grew up watching his father play, now it is his children who watch him. As for whether they will follow in his footsteps, he is clear: "I just want them to be happy and do what they love." Finally, the goalkeeper recalled that he was close to facing his brother Gianfranco when he had just joined Rayo and his brother was a goalkeeper at Almeria. Paulo played that match, but his brother wasn’t there. "I would have liked to have my brother in front of me, but well, it’s difficult." Now, if another opportunity arises, he knows the decision isn’t his: "In the end, it doesn’t depend on us; it depends on the coaches, on the team." This situation could happen next Tuesday at El Alcoraz. His brother is the goalkeeper for Huesca, the team the red-and-whites will face in the Copa del Rey knockout round.

item.title: Richard Jefferson says there’s a change the NBA needs to make around Thanksgiving
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images Thanksgiving is upon us but NBA fans will be left wanting as there are no games scheduled to take place on November 26, something Richard Jefferson is keen to see change. By comparison, NFL supporters have three blockbuster games to look forward to on Thursday, including a particularly big meeting between the 9-1 Buffalo Bills and the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs. Now, Richard Jefferson has called for the NBA to bring back games on Thanksgiving, saying he ‘mainly’ wants it to happen because football started putting matchups on TV during Christmas Day. Richard Jefferson wants NBA to bring back Thanksgiving games Speaking on the Road Trippin’ Show, he said: “The answer is 100% yes. They should bring back Thanksgiving games. “First of all, the fact that the NFL – listen, I know none of us is going to be working, so yes, it would impact us, but let’s just play the hype. Yes, they should. Why? Because the NFL disrespected us and started trying to have games on Christmas Day. They’re trying to take our audience. They’re trying to mess with us. Christmas Day belongs to us, but if y’all want to play that game, then let’s just start playing hoop games, right? “So now, all of a sudden, when you’re watching whoever versus whoever and the score is 42-7, you can switch the channel and turn on a basketball game. So do I believe in it? Yes, I do, mainly because they want to start messing with Christmas Day.” The NBA, then known as the Basketball Association of America, started showing games on Thanksgiving back in 1946. That tradition lasted until 1982 before eventually returning from 1994 to 2006. There were then no games in 2007 before the NBA scheduled fixtures on the holiday again from 2008 to 2010. However, the NBA lockout in 2011 once again brought a halt to the action on Thanksgiving and there have been no matches since. At present, the ‘Holidays’ section of the league’s Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) does not actually make any reference to the November holiday, instead only referencing Christmas, New Year’s and Good Friday. In turn, even if some inside the NBA may wish for it to return, they may find it difficult to get players to agree to a change in schedule. item.title: ‘Dana’s not gonna like this’ – Fans expect UFC response to Carlos Ulberg vs Navajo Stirling statement
item.description: Photo by Mat Hayward/Getty Images Dana White has been critical of teammates not wanting to fight each other in the past. This past weekend’s UFC main event in Qatar brought this topic up due to Navajo Stirling stopping Jiri Prochazka to earn his fourth win and finish of the year. While he’s quickly become the most exciting rising light heavyweight contender, the 205-pound gold is held by his City Kickboxing teammate, Carlos Ulberg. Their coach addressed this situation in an interview to clarify that a fight between them won’t happen, which has fans predicting how White and the UFC will respond. Fans are convinced that Dana White will be critical of Eugene Bareman’s comments City Kickboxing head coach Eugene Bareman completely ruled out the chances of Carlos Ulberg and Navajo Stirling fighting each other. He said, while standing alongside both of his fighters when speaking to the New Zealand Herald, that there is a precedent for this in the UFC so his stance isn’t unique. That doesn’t mean that Dana White will agree with Bareman considering that he’s been very vocal in the past about not liking it when members of the roster say there are certain opponents they won’t fight. Various comments like ‘Dana White’s gonna love this,’ and ‘Something tells me Dana’s not gonna like this’ anticipated how the UFC president will react. Bareman’s comments did receive some support due to him speaking about the bond that exists between Ulberg and Stirling and how that’s bigger than fighting. Others, however, are actively rooting for a strong response from White and the UFC, with some suggesting that ‘Dana should strip Ulberg’. Various posts added that the leading MMA promotion’s boss may already be planning a way around this, saying, ‘Dana White always finds a way.’ Fans suggest that Dana White will force City Kickboxing into an awkward position While one comment underneath the post of Eugene Bareman’s interview said, ‘For once, I hope Dana does something,’ others theorized what his plan could be. Various posts, most of which were comical, suggested that the UFC could have Navajo Stirling fight Magomed Ankalaev for an interim title. This then opens up the possibility of Carlos Ulberg having to fight his teammate in a title unification bout once he is able to compete again. Bareman said in the interview that the UFC punishing Ulberg for this stance isn’t a concern to him because he doesn’t think the promotion will offer this fight when they know it won’t happen. item.title: Bruno Fernandes refuses to close the door on Sporting return as Manchester United contract talks pause
item.description: Bruno Fernandes refuses to close the door on Sporting return as Manchester United contract talks pause Bruno Fernandes has refused to rule out a return to Sporting CP, insisting the door to his former club has never been closed. The Manchester United captain spoke after scoring both of his side's goals in Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting in Lisbon, his first trip back to the club he left for Old Trafford in January 2020. Fernandes spent two-and-a-half seasons with Sporting before moving to the Premier League , and scored 64 goals in 137 games. His comments come amid uncertainty over his future. Fernandes' contract runs out at the end of this season, although United can trigger an option to keep him until June 2028. The 32-year-old has paused talks over a new deal as United focus on improving results. The club are 19th in the Premier League with one win from 11 games, and appointed Mauricio Pochettino as manager last week after parting ways with Michael Carrick. Asked by Sport TV whether he could one day return to Sporting, Fernandes made clear the idea still appeals to him. "[The door] has never been closed. As I've said before, Sporting holds a very special place in my heart -- and it always will."Whether or not it could actually happen depends a great deal on the current manager, the president, and many others wanting it to come to fruition -- myself included, obviously." - Bruno Fernandes to Sport TV Fernandes rejects the idea that players should never go back "But I'm not closing that door, and I never will, because I was very happy here. I don't share the view held by many players who say, 'I don't go back to a place where you were once happy'; I believe that because I was happy here [at Sporting,] I could be happy here again, should the opportunity arise." The Portugal international is closing in on seven years at United since his move to Manchester for an initial £47m fee. During that time, he has won the Europa League, the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup, while being named Manchester United's Player of the Season on a record five occasions.

item.title: NFL Gross Quarterback Rankings: A not-so-fond farewell for Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Six teams were on their bye in Week 11. That meant six quarterbacks got the chance to figure their stuff out. For a backup thrust into the spotlight like Tommy DeVito, that means trying to reclaim the glory of his most meme-able plays. For Michael Penix Jr., it means grinding tape and tweaking a playbook that's seen him tantalize Atlanta Falcons fans before balancing big plays with gruesome mistakes. And for everyone else, it meant ignoring those guys and trying to figure out what the hell is going on in Pittsburgh . Aaron Rodgers makes what could be his final appearance in these rankings after (gestures broadly) . But who else was gross enough to join him in Week 11? There's no perfect metric for a quarterback's impact, but expected points added (EPA) helps measure their ability to swing the outcome of a game through the air, on the ground and through avoiding negative plays. Last year, EPA told us Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford were a cut above the rest of the league's quarterbacks in the regular season, netting 151.3 and 120.3 EPA , respectfully. No one else in the league topped triple digits. Unsurprisingly, those two led playoff teams and finished second and first, respectively, in MVP voting. We can use EPA to help dissect which quarterbacks underwhelmed the hardest in their debut. By comparing their Week 11 EPA across their early 2026 season averages, we get a better idea of whose fans should be most annoyed. And so, we end up with a "worst QBs" list that doesn't include some of the league's actual worst quarterbacks, simply because their starts to the season have been so disappointing we've been moderately conditioned not to expect more this fall. You have to be at least decent in 2026 — or otherworldly awful on a given week — to wind up in the gross QB rankings. We'll also look at completion percentage over expected (CPOE), which gives you a good idea of which quarterbacks are making tough throws (and, in some cases, being bailed out by exceptional catches). All data come from NFL Pro. We'll also keep a running tally of the times each quarterback lands here. We'll score that placement track meet style — 10 points for first place, then eight, six, four, two and one — in order to figure out who was truly 2026's grossest passer. Honorable mention: Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears 2026 EPA/game : 4.7 Week 11 EPA : 1.6 Difference : 3.1 points worse 2026 CPOE : Three percent Week 11 CPOE : 3.1 percent Difference : 0.1 points better Williams is a victim of a week heavy on byes and light on truly disappointing performances. While it was slightly alarming to see the New Orleans Saints' 24th-ranked defense bottle him up, he still got a win that keeps Chicago's momentum rolling into a Thanksgiving showdown with the Detroit Lions. His receiving corps remains an exercise in patience, but there wasn't too much to worry about here. 5. Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 EPA/game : -5.9 Week 11 EPA : -13.2 Difference : 7.3 points worse 2026 CPOE : -1.

item.title: Barnsley players 'letting the badge down' - McGeehan
item.description: Cameron McGeehan has scored nine goals in 17 appearances in all competitions this season [Shutterstock] Barnsley captain Cameron McGeehan says the players are "consumed" by the team's poor form. The Reds are winless in the league since 2 September and are four points adrift of the safety line at the bottom of League One. Their run of 11 league games without a win is their second longest below the top two divisions in their history. "It's our lives, we take it home with us and you don't really switch off, especially at times like this, it consumes you," the midfielder told BBC Radio Sheffield. "We're letting the badge down at the minute and you wear that every day and try and put it right." The South Yorkshire side have taken just one point from their past eight matches. Some travelling fans chanted that the players were "not fit to wear the shirt" after Tuesday's 3-0 defeat at Bradford City. McGeehan, 31, said the team were trying to "draw a line in the sand" from that match when they travel to Wimbledon on Saturday. "It's never nice but we are putting it right and we've got a massive game on Saturday and we're trying to draw a line in the sand and say no more," he added. "We just need to bring it back to winning a game and try and get the fans back on side because we need them more than ever. "They've been great, they've stuck with us and we know we haven't been good enough and results haven't been good. We can completely understand their frustration." 'Boring' talking about good performances Despite the 3-0 scoreline, Barnsley had 23 shots to Bradford's 10 on Tuesday and their previous five defeats to that had all come in 2-1 losses. McGeehan, who returned to the club for a second spell in the summer, said the team were not turning performances into points. "Everyone keeps saying 'that was a good performance' and it's boring talking about that, we need to find a way of being better at getting results," he said. "You saw the other night we had all the ball and we're not making the most of it in terms of scoring and conceding. "It's more frustrating because you think there's a good team in there and a lot of potential but putting that into points is the biggest thing and we're trying to figure that out and get it going as quickly as possible." item.title: LeBron James reveals why he doesn’t ‘dominate every night’ for the Philadelphia 76ers
item.description: Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images LeBron James knows his role with the Philadelphia 76ers, but against the Miami Heat, he definitely got the green light, which led to his first triple-double with the franchise. The 41-year-old scored 25 points, grabbed 10 rebounds and made 12 assists in the 76ers’ 111-104 win against the Heat, who had won seven games in a row leading up to the game. He looked in great rhythm, as he shot 60% from the field and went 4-for-6 from three-point range. In a game where Joel Embiid was absent and Jaylen Brown went down due to an injury in the third quarter, LBJ knew that he had to take over the game if the 76ers needed the win. However, the four-time NBA champion made an interesting point to explain why these kind of performances would be rare for him with the 76ers. LeBron James outlines why he is not dominating every game for the Philadelphia 76ers When James chose Philly as his destination, fans in the city were extremely happy, as the franchise had added an all-time great player to an already strong roster. There were reservations about how things were going to work out with James, Brown, Embiid and Tyrese Maxey all needing the ball. But the 76ers have figured it out, and it has needed James to take a role behind the other stars. “I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club. We have a Finals MVP, regular season MVP, we got an up and coming superstar point guard, a young fella in V.J., who is up and coming as well. My dues are paid and all done; if they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that, but that’s not my job. But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment,” said James to the media. James led the game in +/- and looked phenomenal from start to finish. After the game, Tyrese Maxey was made aware of James’ comments, and he said: “Dust it off then.” This shows that the players on the 76ers are prepared to allow James to play his game when he wants to. Even when he plays a secondary role, the all-time points record holder is making big plays for the team, which is why he is a piece that will be instrumental to them if they are to end their wait for an NBA championship. item.title: Thanksgiving night sky 2026 — What to look for after dinner tonight
item.description: null If your household is like most American families, then on Thursday you likely will all be sitting down with family and friends for a traditional Thanksgiving turkey dinner during the mid-to-late afternoon hours. Then as darkness falls, some will probably migrate into the living room to catch some football or other holiday fare on television. But if you have a large gathering of family and friends at your home — and if your skies are mainly clear — why not invite everyone outside to gaze at the evening sky? If you have binoculars, or better yet, a telescope, you just might end up turning this into a memorable family tradition of its own. First, the "Lord of the Rings" . . . If I may paraphrase the mysterious voice from the 1989 movie, "Field of Dreams": "If you set up your telescope, they will come." And you'll get a big kick out of your Turkey Day guests uttering all the "oohs" and "ahs" or exclamations of "Wow!" with just one peek through the eyepiece. As darkness falls, Saturn will glow at first magnitude, shining with a sedate, yellow-white light and appearing noticeably brighter than the star Fomalhaut, about 40 degrees (the equivalent of four fist-widths) to its lower right. Its famous ring system is now tilted only about six degrees toward Earth but may be visible with steadied (or image-stabilized) high-power binoculars or through the eyepiece of a telescope magnifying over 30-power. The rings will seem to glow with an inner light and for those who have never had the pleasure of seeing them for themselves, that first view always elicits astonishment; kids especially most often will say: "Awesome!" or "No way!" I've even had people accuse me of using a slide of Saturn, to which I, of course, reply with, "No . . . that's the real thing." Saturn will shine high in the southern sky on Nov. 26. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) . . . and later, the moon Then, along about 6:25 p.m. local time, the waning gibbous moon, 2½ days past full phase and 91% illuminated, will begin to emerge from beyond the east-northeast horizon. Give it another hour and it will stand about 10 degrees above the horizon — equal to the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. By then, the moon will be in a better position for evening study. Location of the moon at approximately 9p.m. on Thanksgiving. Local moonrise and moonset times will vary depending on your location. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8 ) Even in binoculars, the moon is a striking sight to see. It's such a special object because it doesn't matter whether you live in a rural area or in the middle of a brightly lit city, for the moon can always be readily observed. It always looks spectacular whether you're using binoculars or a telescope. It never looks precisely the same no matter how often you view it and can be observed even on hazy or partially cloud-covered nights. item.title: Remembering Pete Edochie: 5 Films That Made Him a Nollywood Legend
item.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Pete Edochie and Genevieve Nnaji behind the scenes on the set of the 2018 film Lionheart, where they played father and daughter Chief Ernest Obiagu and Adaeze Obiagu. Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. Things Fall Apart (1987) Before Nollywood’s home-video boom even began, Pete Edochie became a household name across Nigeria and internationally through his breakout role as Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel Things Fall Apart. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. Rituals (1997) As Nollywood entered its golden home-video era in the late 1990s, Edochie starred in Andy Amenechi’s gripping thriller Rituals as Don Pedro, a calculating member of a secretive and ruthless society. item.description: For Ece Temelkuran, the human condition is "unhomed". item.title: 19 years after, Olajumoke’s hostels for disabled students decay
item.description: — Invaded by bedbugs, broken doors, faulty drains — Students seek urgent intervention as AAUA VC promises action By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Nineteen years after former Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Senator Bode Olajumoke, donated two hostels for students with disabilities, the facilities have fallen into a state of disrepair, with residents appealing to the university authorities for urgent intervention. Olajumoke, who visited the male and female hostels he donated in February 2006, expressed dismay at their condition, describing the facilities as horrible and neglected. Conducted round the buildings by the hostel manager, Joseph Aladegbola, the former senator said the living conditions of the students were unacceptable and urged the university management to urgently rehabilitate the facilities. Olajumoke donated the hostels after discovering that the institution had no accommodation specifically designed for students with disabilities. The two buildings, alongside an office for the hostel manager, were commissioned by former Senate President, Senator Ken Nnamani, with the late Governor Olusegun Agagu as guest of honour. They were purpose-built to accommodate students with physical disabilities, with wide doors and toilets and bathrooms designed to allow wheelchair access. However, the hostel manager attributed the poor state of the facilities to inadequate funding, saying the hostels received maintenance funds at most twice a year, an allocation he described as insufficient to address their needs. After inspecting the buildings, Olajumoke visited the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Tomola Obamuyi, where he raised concerns about the level of deterioration. He warned that the unhygienic conditions could trigger disease outbreaks if urgent steps were not taken to address them. Olajumoke said the male hostel was in a worse condition, adding that both buildings had been invaded by bedbugs and required immediate fumigation. He called on stakeholders to work together to improve the living conditions of students with disabilities. One of the students lamented that the rooms, bathrooms, toilets and kitchen were all in a state of neglect. “The institution has neglected the hostels, the toilets are bad, doors and windows falling, all other facilities are in deplorable conditions,” the student said. The student appealed to the university authorities to restore the buildings to the condition they were in when Olajumoke donated them. Also speaking, a former hall chairman, Joseph Agada, urged the university management to prioritise the renovation of the hostels before the situation deteriorated further. Agada called for comprehensive repairs, including the replacement of damaged bathroom and toilet facilities, provision of new chairs and fumigation to tackle the bedbug infestation. “We need the complete renovation of the two hostels, new chairs, the fumigation of the hostels because of the invasion of bedbugs. item.title: Succession Battle: Court issues arrest warrant against Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: By Henry Ojelu A Lagos State High Court sitting in Ikoyi has issued a bench warrant for the arrest of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya over his failure to appear in court in a contempt case arising from the leadership crisis at the Fountain of Life Church. Justice O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the warrant on Thursday following Odukoya’s absence from proceedings in a suit instituted by the Incorporated Trustees of the church. The judge also directed that the case file be returned to the administrative judge for reassignment. The development followed an earlier order issued on November 18, restraining Odukoya from parading himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head or interfering with its governance, administration and activities. The order was granted following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as its Senior Pastor. The faction cited a review of the church’s constitution and a video recording allegedly containing succession instructions left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. According to the trustees, the recording, made in December 2021, showed that the late cleric had preferred Pastor Kunle Areogun as his successor, while assigning Jimmy an administrative role and responsibility for the church’s youth ministry. They claimed the recording was not presented when Jimmy was appointed Senior Pastor in September 2023, following his father’s death. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, Odukoya rejected his removal, insisting that it was not based on a valid decision of the church’s recognised Board of Trustees. He maintained that his appointment in 2023 was unanimously approved and that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor. The dispute also resulted in a suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos, where Odukoya and the church’s Incorporated Trustees challenged the validity of resolutions allegedly taken by some members of the board. The suit named his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church members as defendants. Speaking during a church service on November 22, Odukoya said he had heard about the restraining order but had not been served with the court documents. “I heard there was an injunction against me. I heard, but I have not seen it, and I have not been served. They said that there was no substituted service. Legally, I have not been served,” he said. He also reassured members of the congregation, declaring: “You know there is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life, and as long as you would have me, I will continue to speak for you.” The Fountain of Life Church was founded in 1992 by the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya and his wife, Bimbo. item.description: Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of exploiting poverty to attract voters, saying the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) relies on what he described as the “weaponisation of poverty’s algorithm” for political engagement. Bwala also accused the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, (NDC) Peter Obi, of relying heavily on social media engagement to sustain his political popularity, insisting that online activities and large crowds at rallies were not reliable indicators of electoral strength. He spoke on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast while reacting to questions about whether Tinubu was worried by the growing support for Atiku in the North ahead of the January 16 presidential election. Bwala dismissed the crowds at Atiku’s campaign rallies as insufficient evidence of widespread voter support, arguing that the former vice-president had a history of attracting large audiences during campaigns without translating such gatherings into electoral victories. “I am an advocate from day one that numbers in rally is not a proof of popularity. I even cautioned people from our own side that if we go to a place and everywhere is filled, let us not project it as a strength, because we dey on the street we know how people are gathered in campaigns and Atiku is a master in gathering people when it comes to campaign,” he said. Recalling Atiku’s presidential contest against former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Bwala said the former vice-president gained significant momentum shortly before the election, with large crowds creating the impression that he could defeat the incumbent. He, however, said the rally attendance did not translate into victory, arguing that grassroots mobilisation and actual voter support were more important than crowd size. “I remember the first time he ran on the platform provided by Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu against Obasanjo. It was within few days to election that he was sort of getting some oxygen. If you see everywhere he goes, rave, rave, rave. Everybody believed he was going to defeat Obasanjo. At the end of the day, what is it?” Bwala said. He said genuine political strength should be measured by a candidate’s ability to mobilise voters at the grassroots rather than the number of people attending campaign rallies. Bwala also questioned Atiku’s political structure in the North, asking what support system the former vice-president had in the region, particularly as the party he recently joined had no governor. “But even with the crowd, we have pulled more crowds than him. So what is Atiku Tsunami? What is his structure? Because right now the party he has moved to does not have a governor,” he said. The presidential aide also criticised Obi’s political strategy, claiming that the former Anambra governor’s popularity was largely sustained by social media activities rather than physical political struct

item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Survivors, families recount horror
item.description: …Seven members of one family among victims …Bereaved relatives ask: How do we recover? …Ukubie community appeals for access road By Emem Idio, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled desperately for survival after an overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat unfit to carry the large number of passengers on board. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but a local boat was eventually provided when none was available. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after they boarded, raising concerns among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from side to side, prompting passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, triggering panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. When she resurfaced, she said she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, ostensibly to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young woman die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she became particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said: “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she saved herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son

item.title: Microsoft hotpatches hotpatch that could crash Windows Server 2025
item.description: Microsoft has released an out-of-band hotpatch to fix a bug in November's Windows Server 2025 security update that could crash some servers when an IPv6 route expires. The patch for the patch, KB5138318 , addresses crashes on systems with Router Advertisement (RA) enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes. When a route timer expires, affected servers can halt with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE). Issued on November 25, the corrective update takes effect without requiring a restart, according to Microsoft. KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE means the kernel has detected corruption of a critical data structure and stopped the system. Microsoft has identified route-timer expiry as the trigger but hasn't explained the underlying coding fault. Good to see the operating system being protected against the impact of the corruption. Less good for administrators wondering why their servers have suddenly misbehaved. Lansweeper puts Windows Server 2025 at 7 percent of the servers it monitors, compared with 32 percent for Server 2022 and 33 percent for Server 2019. Only systems with the affected hotpatch and networking configuration are implicated. Microsoft's Windows Server updates have not gone well over the last few months, with out-of-band updates issued in September, October, and November. An out-of-band update to deal with a problem introduced in a hotpatch (in this case, KB5131077 ) therefore carries with it a certain sense of inevitability. Hotpatches are a way of getting OS security updates on a Windows Server without requiring a restart and so are, in theory, a boon for administrators keen on maximizing uptime. According to Microsoft, in addition to faster installations and better protection, there is "lower workload impact with less need to restart your machine." Avoiding a planned restart is less of a selling point when the alternative is an unplanned crash. ®

item.title: Thailand–Nigeria trade hits $1.88bn in nine months
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Thailand’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Thirapath Mongkolnavin, has said trade between the two countries rose by 104.73 per cent to about $1.88 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with the same period last year. Mongkolnavin disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja at a reception marking Thailand’s National Day, Father’s Day and the birth anniversary of the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej. The envoy said Thailand would expand economic and development cooperation with Nigeria and other African countries through its Thailand–Africa Initiative. He said the two countries would mark 65 years of diplomatic relations in 2027, adding that the August visit of Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs to Nigeria and the first bilateral consultations had opened new opportunities for cooperation. He said, “In the economic sphere, our bilateral trade reached approximately USD 1.88 billion during the first nine months of this year, representing a remarkable 104.73 percent increase year-on-year.” Nigeria’s Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Dunoma Umar Ahmed, called for the early conclusion of agreements on investment promotion, air services, visa facilitation and judicial cooperation. Ahmed said the agreements would create more opportunities for trade, investment and tourism. He singled out improved air connectivity as a way to bring businesses and people in both countries closer. He said, “In particular, improved air connectivity between our two countries would serve as a vital link in bringing our peoples, businesses and economies closer together.” Ahmed said the Technical Cooperation Agreement signed during the August visit had opened opportunities for skills development, training and technical exchanges. He identified agriculture, manufacturing, renewable energy, tourism and technology as areas where both countries could expand cooperation. Mongkolnavin said Thailand continued to offer Nigerians scholarships and training through the Thailand International Cooperation Agency’s Annual International Training Course and Thailand International Postgraduate Programme. He said he hoped to use his position as Thailand’s first ambassador to the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, to promote closer dialogue and cooperation between the bloc and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, ASEAN. Ahmed also reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to the safety and welfare of Thai nationals living in the country and thanked Thailand for its support for Nigerians living there. At the reception, the Thai Embassy organised a “Chud Thai” AI photo exhibition to promote Thailand’s traditional attire ahead of its consideration for inscription on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The interactive booth allowed guests to see themselves wearing Chud Thai in AI-generated photographs. Mongkolnavin also paid tribute to the late Queen Sirikit, the Queen M

item.title: ICE arrests undocumented immigrant days after winning $1m lottery
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has arrested a Salvadoran man in Massachusetts, a week after he won $1 million in a state lottery. The agency’s Boston office said officers arrested Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales in East Boston on Tuesday, following a brief foot chase, according to Fox News. Velasquez-Morales entered the United States in 2013, but an immigration judge ordered his removal from the country the following year. In a statement posted on social media, ICE said his lottery win led to his arrest. The agency also shared a photograph of the Salvadoran man holding an oversized cheque after collecting his prize at the Massachusetts Lottery headquarters in Dorchester, a neighbourhood in Boston. Velasquez-Morales won the prize through the “$2,000,000 50X Cashword” crossword-style scratch ticket game. His name appeared on the cheque as “Ariel Velasquez.” Reacting to the arrest, ICE’s Boston office wrote: “Welcome to the ERO Boston lottery! Where illegal aliens and sanctuary politicians are out of luck, and the law-abiding citizens of New England are always the winners!” In a separate statement, the agency said: “the rights and privileges reserved for American citizens are for American citizens, NOT illegal aliens. The patriots of ICE continue to work around the clock to enforce our nation’s laws and serve the American people.” A 2009 study by the University of Michigan found that 43.9 per cent of undocumented immigrants surveyed participated in lottery or scratch-ticket games. The research, which involved 431 respondents, examined gambling as a form of entertainment and relief among immigrants without permanent legal status. Velasquez-Morales’ arrest came amid renewed attention on the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement, following the departure of another Salvadoran migrant, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, from the United States. item.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
item.description: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it. A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note. Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO 2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO 2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO 2 . That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane. Read full article Comments

item.title: PTAD unveils N5bn health scheme, announces N180bn pension payments
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young LAGOS — The Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) has unveiled a N5 billion health insurance scheme for retirees under the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS), while announcing over N180 billion in pension-related payments and interventions in the last two years. The Executive Secretary of PTAD, Tolulope Odunaiya, disclosed this on Thursday at a stakeholder engagement forum in Lagos, where she outlined the Directorate’s achievements in pension administration, including the settlement of inherited pension liabilities, payment of pension increment arrears and introduction of digital reforms to improve service delivery. Odunaiya said the N5 billion intervention culminated in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS pensioners, which was formally unveiled at the event. “Most significantly, we secured funding of approximately N5 billion for a major healthcare intervention, culminating in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS Pensioners, which we are unveiling today,” she said. She explained that the scheme was designed to address retirees’ healthcare needs, stressing that their welfare extended beyond the regular payment of monthly pensions. “This initiative reflects our recognition that Pensioners’ welfare extends beyond the timely payment of monthly pension entitlements. Access to free, quality, and reliable healthcare is fundamental to their well-being and quality of life,” she added. On pension liabilities, the Executive Secretary disclosed that PTAD had settled over N91.5 billion in inherited obligations, including N25.05 billion paid to 9,675 former employees of the defunct Nigerian Telecommunications Limited (NITEL) and its mobile subsidiary, MTEL, as final settlement of outstanding entitlements. She also said over N60 billion had been paid in arrears arising from the N32,000 pension increment, benefiting more than 150,000 eligible pensioners. In addition, the Directorate paid over N23.8 billion in arrears arising from pension increments of 10.66 per cent, 12.95 per cent, 13.8 per cent and 20.55 per cent, alongside the implementation of corresponding increases in monthly pensions. On pension harmonisation, Odunaiya said PTAD had disbursed over N5 billion in arrears to more than 64,000 eligible pensioners. She added that over 30,000 pensioners had benefited from monthly pension re-computation, with N3.8 billion paid in associated arrears. The Executive Secretary further announced that 726 retirees had been enrolled on the pension payroll, comprising 508 former employees of the Federal Mortgage Finance Limited (FMFL) and 218 retirees of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). The new beneficiaries attract a combined monthly pension obligation of over N41 million, she said. item.title: ‘Completely unacceptable’: Kimmich blasts Bayern over Musiala treatment
item.description: Bayern Munich vice-captain Joshua Kimmich has hit out at the club’s hierarchy for pressuring Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Speaking after a Champions League defeat at Lille on Wednesday, the Germany skipper — who is Bayern’s captain with Manuel Neuer currently injured — became the latest to criticise the German giants. “Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than the players, but it is not bigger than the person,” Kimmich said. “It’s completely unacceptable and is not the Bayern way… What’s happening now is something that must not happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.” In August, Musiala collapsed twice on the field in pre-season games and then revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Musiala played last Friday in his first match since a two-month absence with an unrelated hamstring injury. Moments after the match, long-time club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge said the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form and should accept a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Honorary president Uli Hoeness and current club chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen have made similar statements. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension in February 2025. According to German media reports, he earns 25 million euros ($27 million) per season, making Musiala the club’s second-highest paid player after Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. On Sunday, international players’ union FIFPRO accused Bayern of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Kimmich said he understood the club’s position but was critical of the decision to go public. “I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal’s agent or with Jamal himself,” Kimmich said. Kimmich missed several games in October after the sudden death of his father and said he appreciated the support of the club during that time. “In my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out,” Kimmich added. Wednesday’s defeat to Lille ended Bayern’s run as the last club in Europe’s top-five leagues yet to suffer defeat in any competition. item.title: Lagos govt, UNICEF, NGE seek action on child welfare
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh LAGOS — The Lagos State Government, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) and other stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The call was made on Thursday at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, themed: “Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility.” The event was organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME), with participation from Airtel Nigeria and other stakeholders. Speaking at the symposium, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, said ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential was a collective responsibility that should not be left to government alone. Citing a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, Anaba described the figure as alarming and called for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to assess their contributions towards addressing the challenge. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms Lone Hvass, said Nigeria’s future would be determined by the decisions made today to protect and invest in its children. She said child survival, education and learning were interconnected, noting that children excluded from school were also denied opportunities for protection, participation and the realisation of their potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said the welfare of children required sustained commitment from government, parents, caregivers, development partners and the media. She said children should not be regarded merely as beneficiaries of government policies but as individuals with rights, aspirations, talents and op

item.title: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 5 (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe, Sporting CP striker Luis Suarez and Como attacker Anastasios Douvikas are jointly leading the UEFA Champions League scoring chart after the conclusion of Matchday 5. The trio have each scored six goals in the competition this season, maintaining a narrow lead over a group of players who have found the net five times. Mbappe strengthened his position with a brace in Real Madrid’s 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday. Suarez also scored twice in Sporting CP’s 2-2 draw against Manchester United, taking his tally to six goals, while Douvikas remains on the same number. item.title: UK government working 'around the clock' on Capita contingency plans
item.description: The UK government is working "around the clock" on contingency plans for Capita contracts after the outsourcer's CEO quit and its shares plunged, a Cabinet Office minister told MPs. Capita announced plans this week to raise around £190 million through a share issue in the first half of 2027 after warning of sharply lower profits and further costs linked to its Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract. The outsourcer "should be absolutely ashamed of its performance" on the £239 million contract , Sally Jameson, parliamentary secretary in the Cabinet Office, told MPs on Tuesday . "We have seen evidence that it has stepped up in recent months and begun to rectify the problem, but it is inexcusable that it let the situation get to this point," she said. Adolfo Hernandez stepped down as CEO with immediate effect on Monday, with finance chief Pablo Andres taking over. Shares fell around 70 percent following the announcement. In the House of Commons, Jameson was asked about the government's plans if Capita were unable to carry out the remainder of its contract given the outsourcer's performance on the CSPS. "On contingency planning, it is important that we stabilize the situation and that Capita can continue to deliver the pension scheme. However, the government is working across departments, as we do in relation to all strategic suppliers, to ensure that the relevant contingency plans are in place. People are working around the clock on that," she said. Jameson said contingency planning for the pension scheme was already underway before Monday's announcement, describing it as standard practice for major government suppliers. She told the Chamber that the Cabinet Office was "currently arranging to meet the new CEO in the coming days" following Hernandez's departure. The Register first exposed problems with Capita's CSPS portal last December. The site, serving 1.5 million current and former public servants, rejected login details even for newly created accounts, contained broken and circular links, and displayed dummy text. In January this year, the Cabinet Office was forced to promise "interim support measures" for the CSPS following Capita's botched takeover, including 150 additional government staff to clear the backlog in cases. Speaking in Parliament, Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the Public Accounts Committee, said there had been "some tragic and dreadful cases" since Capita took over administration last December. "I heard of one poor lady who was living on benefits because she could not get the bereavement payments she needed after her sister's death. I have heard of a member of parliamentary staff, not far from this Chamber, who is having to delay his retirement by a year because he cannot even get a statement from the scheme." The government has withheld nearly £10 million in contractual payments over Capita's performance. It is currently locked in negotiations over further penalties following the appointment of an auditor
